接.meaning: On a sinking ship, a <part>woman</part> hugs the <part>anchor</part> and rides it down to the sea floor, where she plants her feet to <part>stand</part>. She reaches out one finger to a sleeping whale's nose. Just one tiny <kanji>touch</kanji>, and the whale opens an eye.
接.on: The whale yawns, and out swims a soggy red <sound>set</sound>ter, paddling for the surface.
接.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the whale, and a stream of bubbles joins it to the boat above.

参.meaning: A <part>large</part> walrus with droopy <part>whiskers</part> knocks on your door with one <part>elbow</part>, because his flippers are full of fish. He's come all the way from the ice for tea. It's his yearly <kanji>visit</kanji>.
参.on: He brings you an ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae, with a sardine on top.
参.kun: '<sound>My</sound>, what a big guest!' says Grandma, as he squeezes in through the door.

追.meaning: A <part>snowman</part> on a tea tray shoots down a long icy <part>ramp</part> after his own carrot nose, which bounced off when he sneezed. Faster and faster he slides, stick arms flailing, gaining on it inch by inch. Nothing will stop him in this <kanji>chase</kanji>.
追.on: At the bottom he finally pinches the runaway carrot with a pair of <sound>twee</sound>zers and pops it back on his face.
追.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the snowman as the carrot slips from his grip again and skids off downhill, and away he goes after it.

抜.meaning: Your <part>friend</part> is wedged tight in a narrow cave, so you hook a ship's <part>anchor</part> to her boots and let a passing tugboat tow it. The rope twangs, the rock groans, and with a loud pop she shoots free. She's managed to <kanji>slip out</kanji>.
抜.on: As she pops free, a <sound>butt</sound>on flies off her coat and pings off the tugboat's horn.
抜.kun: Still dizzy, she crawls into a cosy <sound>noo</sound>k on the deck to catch her breath.

害.meaning: A storm tears the <part>TV antenna</part> off the <part>roof</part>, and it drops straight into the wide <part>mouth</part> of a man yawning on the porch below. One chipped tooth, one bent antenna, no signal for the match. The storm did a lot of <kanji>harm</kanji>.
害.on: His <sound>gui</sound>de dog drags the bent antenna far out into the garden, growling at it as if it were a burglar.

職.meaning: Your new job: stand beside the <part>war gong</part> all day with one <part>ear</part> pressed against it, listening for the faint hum that means trouble is coming over the hills. It's dull, but it pays, and nobody else wants it. It's your <kanji>post</kanji>.
職.on: One day you lean in too close just as someone strikes it, and the boom hits you like an electric <sound>shock</sound>.

未.meaning: A young <part>tree</part> has sprouted one short new branch above its old one, still too thin to hold a bird. A sparrow lands, the twig bends, and the sparrow hops off in a huff. Come back next spring: it's <kanji>not yet</kanji> ready.
未.on: Below, a <sound>mee</sound>rkat stands on tiptoe, waiting for the branch to grow strong enough to be its lookout.
未.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, can I perch on it now?' asks the little sparrow. Its mother shakes her head and says it again: not yet.

球.meaning: The <part>king</part> is bored at his birthday feast and makes one <part>request</part>: something round that bounces. The servants search the castle and come back with the golden orb from his crown, which he dribbles down the hall. Finally, a <kanji>ball</kanji>.
球.on: Then he grabs a pool <sound>cue</sound> and sends the golden ball cracking across the throne room into a suit of armour.
球.kun: It rolls under a <sound>ta</sound>co cart in the courtyard, and the king calls for his <sound>ma</sound>ma to fish it out.
